title: South Korea's PIPC completes pre-merger data checks of Korean Air, Gmarket and Remember & Company, finds no violations at Korean Air
date_note: Newsis's article of 26 November reports the commission disclosing the results that day; it was deliberated on 25 November.
geo_basis: country as stated by the source; pin at the capital
summary: South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission said it completed preliminary inspections of Korean Air, Gmarket and Remember & Company, Newsis reports. It found no legal violations or unauthorised leaks at Korean Air and no unauthorised provision of data to Remember's largest shareholder or affiliates. It urged Gmarket to strengthen oversight of processors, recommended Asiana destroy its data once its purpose is fulfilled, and issued transfer guidance.
plain: South Korea's data protection regulator checked three companies undergoing mergers or ownership changes. Newsis reports it found no violations at Korean Air and issued guidance for data transfers in mergers.
exec: The regulator issued guidance on moving personal data in mergers and asked Gmarket to tighten oversight of its data processors, Newsis reports.

validation.note: One publisher (Newsis) relaying the commission's announcement; the commission's own release was not read.

review.note: stronger than the source: no violations or leaks was stated only for Korean Air; Remember had no unauthorised provision; Gmarket got an oversight recommendation. Dropped 'so far'. Title, summary, plain and exec now scoped per company.
